items.objective_statement: discuss how the methodology employed by Galileo contributed to the development of Physics
items.stem: Galileo's contribution to the study of falling bodies was that he

options.text: argued from what heavy bodies ought to do

misconception.label: That is the approach Galileo argued against.

options.text: timed falling bodies and let the measurements decide
proved that heavy bodies fall faster than light ones

misconception.label: His measurements showed the opposite, once air resistance is allowed for.

options.text: showed that bodies fall only in a vacuum

misconception.label: Bodies fall in air as well; the vacuum only removes air resistance.

steps: Before Galileo, motion was argued from what a body ought to do.
Galileo measured the motion of falling and rolling bodies and drew his conclusion from the readings.
That is the experimental method the syllabus credits him with.
solution.answer_line: timed falling bodies and let the measurements decide

items.objective_statement: draw a line of ‘best fit’ for a set of plotted values
items.stem: A line of best fit is a better description of a set of readings than a line joining the points because the best fit line

misconception.label: Being easier to draw is not a reason for preferring it.

options.text: averages out the uncertainty in the individual readings

misconception.label: Only a relationship of direct proportion passes through the origin.

options.text: is always steeper than the joined line

misconception.label: The gradient of the best fit line is whatever the readings give; it is not systematically steeper.

steps: Every reading carries a small error, so no single point is exactly right.
Joining the points repeats those errors in the shape of the line.
A single line drawn with the points balanced above and below it averages the errors out, so its gradient is the best estimate available.
solution.answer_line: averages out the uncertainty in the individual readings

items.stem: The reading of the caliper, in mm, is

misconception.label: Read only the main scale and ignored the vernier altogether.
Read the number of the vernier division that lines up as if it were the whole reading.

steps: Read the main scale at the vernier zero: it lies between 3 and 4, so the whole number of millimetres is 3.
Find the vernier division that lines up exactly with a main scale mark. It is the sixth.

The reading is 3 + 0.6 = 3.6 mm.

items.stem: The density of a substance is defined as its

misconception.label: That is the reciprocal of the density.

items.stem: A force acting on a body can change the body's

misconception.label: The mass of a body does not depend on the forces acting on it.

items.objective_statement: identify situations in which the application of a force will result in a turning effect
items.stem: A force will produce a turning effect about a point when the force

misconception.label: A force through the point has zero perpendicular distance, so no turning effect.

options.text: acts at a distance from the point

misconception.label: A force in any direction can turn a body, not only a vertical one.

options.text: is larger than the weight of the body

misconception.label: The size of the force compared with the weight is not what decides it.

steps: The moment of a force is the force times the perpendicular distance from the point to its line of action.
If the force passes through the point that distance is zero.
So a turning effect requires the force to act at some distance from the point.
solution.answer_line: acts at a distance from the point

items.stem: The moment of a force about a point is the force multiplied by the

Multiply the force by that perpendicular distance; the moment is quoted in N m and not in joules.

items.stem: In this arrangement the effort is smaller than the load because the effort

options.text: acts in the opposite direction to the load

misconception.label: The directions matter for which moment is clockwise, not for the size of the effort.

options.text: acts further from the pivot than the load does
acts through a smaller distance than the load

misconception.label: The effort moves through the greater distance, not the smaller; that is the cost of the smaller force.

options.text: is applied by two hands rather than one

misconception.label: The number of hands has nothing to do with the moments.

The effort acts 1.60 m from the wheel and the load only 0.40 m.

items.stem: A book rests on a table. The force that balances the weight of the book is the

items.objective_statement: apply the law of conservation of linear momentum
items.stem: The law of conservation of linear momentum applies to a collision provided that

options.text: no external force acts on the colliding bodies

misconception.label: Momentum is conserved in inelastic collisions too.
The masses may be different.
Kinetic energy is not conserved in an inelastic collision, but momentum still is.

steps: The forces the colliding bodies exert on each other are equal and opposite, by Newton's third law.
So the momentum gained by one equals the momentum lost by the other.
This holds whatever kind of collision it is, provided no outside force interferes.
solution.answer_line: no external force acts on the colliding bodies

options.text: potential energy increases and kinetic energy decreases

items.stem: A woman wearing stiletto heels sinks into soft ground more easily than when wearing flat shoes because the stiletto heels

misconception.label: Her weight is the same in either pair of shoes.

options.text: reduce the area in contact with the ground
increase the area in contact with the ground

misconception.label: A larger area would reduce the pressure.
Her weight is the same in either pair of shoes.

steps: Pressure is force per unit area, and her weight is the force in both cases.
The heels put that weight on a very small area.
A smaller area with the same force gives a greater pressure, so the heels sink in.
solution.answer_line: reduce the area in contact with the ground

items.stem: A body floats in a liquid when the upthrust on it is

misconception.label: If the upthrust were greater the body would accelerate upwards.

steps: A floating body is at rest, so the forces on it balance.
The two vertical forces are the weight down and the upthrust up.
So for floating, upthrust = weight.
solution.answer_line: equal to its weight

items.stem: In terms of the kinetic theory, the pressure of a gas increases when it is heated at constant volume because the particles

misconception.label: Particle size does not change with temperature.

misconception.label: There is no attraction towards the walls; the particles simply collide with them.

Faster particles also cross the container more often, so impacts are more frequent.
More force spread over the same wall area means a higher pressure.

items.stem: Cooling a radioactive source to a very low temperature has what effect on its rate of decay?

misconception.label: Chemical reaction rates fall on cooling, but nuclear decay is not a chemical reaction.
Heating does not speed decay up either.
Nothing available in a laboratory stops a nucleus from decaying.

steps: Radioactive decay happens inside the nucleus.
The nucleus is shielded from the outside world by the electrons around it.
So temperature, pressure and chemical combination leave the decay rate untouched.
solution.answer_line: The rate is unchanged
